mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A UNRATE crossing above 4.5% triggers a recession signal, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20d returns not significantly negative (p > 0.05 in t-test) when UNRATE crosses above 4.5%, or returns revert quickly.

mechanism_narrative: Rising demand (GDPC1) and falling FEDFUNDS (easing) jointly boost equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 rises > 2% and FEDFUNDS falls > 1% in a month
failure_condition: No significant positive returns when both proxies move in expected directions (p > 0.05 in multivariate regression).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a drop in FEDFUNDS (easing) strongly predicts positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion, 20d returns not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS falls, or effect diminishes outside the regime.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth not strongly correlated with 60d returns (p > 0.05 in regression), or returns revert before horizon.

mechanism_narrative: Payroll employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 150,000 in a month signals labor market strength, prompting positive S&P 500 returns within 5 days.
failure_condition: 5d returns not significantly positive when PAYEMS crosses threshold (p > 0.05), or effect fades quickly.

mechanism_narrative: Both rising demand (GDPC1) and employment (PAYEMS) indicate economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 rises > 2% and PAYEMS rises > 50,000 in a month
failure_condition: No significant positive returns when both proxies rise as expected (p > 0.05 in multivariate regression).

mechanism_narrative: In post-shock recovery, falling FEDFUNDS and rising demand (GDPC1) both predict positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 rises > 3% and FEDFUNDS falls > 1.5% over 60 days
failure_condition: 60d returns not significantly positive when both proxies move in expected directions (p > 0.05), or effect weakens outside the regime.
